SYNTHETIC TRAINING NOTE — NOT REAL PATIENT DATA
Note Type: Emergency Medicine Provider Note
Author: ED Attending
Date: 2026-05-08

Chief Complaint: Abdominal pain.

HPI: 58-year-old presenting to ED with two days of progressive abdominal
pain, now localized to right lower quadrant. Patient reports nausea and
emesis, no diarrhea, no hematochezia. Tolerated sips of water in triage.

Physical Exam: Alert, in moderate distress from pain. Abdomen with focal
RLQ tenderness, voluntary guarding, no rebound. Negative psoas sign on exam.

Labs: WBC 11.2 with left shift, lipase normal, UA negative for infection.

Assessment and Plan: Acute abdominal pain — differential includes
appendicitis (status post prior appendectomy makes this less likely),
diverticulitis, mesenteric process. Will obtain CT, admit to medicine,
pain control with IV opioid PRN.
